title: My Boss Asked Me to Take His Daughter to Prom and Promised a Reward, Then She Looked Me in the Eyes and Said He Didn't Choose Me by Accident
fb_text:
MY BOSS ASKED ME TO TAKE HIS DAUGHTER TO PROM AND PROMISED TO REWARD ME. I THOUGHT IT WAS A SIMPLE FAVOR UNTIL SHE OPENED THE CAR DOOR, LOOKED ME IN THE EYES, AND SAID, "WAIT. MY DAD DIDN'T CHOOSE YOU BY ACCIDENT. AND IT WASN'T FOR MY SAKE."

I was nineteen when I started working for Sheldon.

I needed that job far more than he probably understood.

My mother was raising my younger sister alone, and money was always tight. I gave Mom part of every paycheck for groceries, bills, and whatever my sister needed for school.

So I was never late.

I never missed a shift unless I truly had no choice.

When Sheldon asked me to stay an extra hour, I stayed.

After a year, I was the one he counted on for everything, from deliveries to locking up at night.

Then one Friday afternoon, he called me into his office.

"I need a favor, Brent."

"Sure."

He hesitated.

"My daughter's prom is tomorrow."

Georgia was eighteen. I had run into her at the office a few times, but we barely knew each other.

"The boy she was going with backed out," Sheldon said. "I want you to take her."

I thought he was joking.

"Me?"

"You're responsible. I trust you."

Then he added, "Do this for me, and I'll make it worth your while."

I thought about how much even a little extra money could ease things for my mom and sister.

"Okay."

The next evening, I borrowed my uncle's car, put on the only suit I owned, and drove to Sheldon's house.

He opened the front door himself.

Strangely, he looked even more nervous than Georgia.

"Just make sure she has a good night," he said.

Then Georgia came down the stairs.

She looked beautiful, but the moment she saw me, her smile vanished.

She hardly said a word while her father took pictures.

The drive to prom was painfully quiet.

I tried to start a conversation. I asked about her friends, what music she liked, and whether she was looking forward to the dance.

She answered in a few words and turned back to the window.

Eventually, I stopped trying.

When we pulled up outside the venue, I turned off the engine.

"Well," I said, forcing a smile. "I hope tonight won't be too awful. I guess your dad really wanted you to go to prom."

Georgia didn't smile back.

She opened the passenger door but didn't get out.

Instead, she turned and looked straight into my eyes.

"Wait."

I looked at her.

"My dad didn't choose you by accident. And it wasn't for my sake."

article_html:
I was nineteen when I started working for Sheldon, and I needed that job far more than he probably understood.

My mother was raising my younger sister on her own, and money was always tight. I gave Mom part of every paycheck for groceries, bills, and anything my sister needed for school.

That was why I was never late. I never missed a shift unless I had no other choice. Whenever Sheldon asked me to stay an extra hour, I stayed. After a year, I was the one he relied on for everything, from making deliveries to locking up at night.

The Favor

One Friday afternoon, he called me into his office.

"I need a favor, Brent."

"Sure."

He paused. "My daughter's prom is tomorrow."

Georgia was eighteen. I had crossed paths with her at the office a handful of times, but we hardly knew each other.

"The boy she was supposed to go with backed out," Sheldon said. "I want you to take her."

I thought he was kidding. "Me?"

"You're responsible. I trust you." Then he added, "Do this for me, and I'll make it worth your while."

I thought of my mom and my sister, and how much even a little extra money could help them.

"Okay."

A Silent Ride

The next evening, I borrowed my uncle's car, put on the only suit I owned, and drove to Sheldon's house. He met me at the door, looking even more anxious than Georgia would later seem.

"Just make sure she has a good night," he said.

Georgia came down the stairs. She looked gorgeous, but the second she saw me, her smile disappeared. She barely spoke while her father took pictures.

The drive was unbearably quiet. I asked about her friends, the music she liked, and whether she was looking forward to the dance. She answered in a few words and turned back to the window. Eventually, I gave up.

When we reached the venue, I switched off the engine.

"Well," I said, forcing a smile. "I hope tonight won't be too terrible. I guess your dad really wanted you to go to prom."

Georgia didn't smile. She opened the passenger door but stayed in her seat. Then she turned and looked straight into my eyes.

"Wait."

I looked at her.

"My dad didn't choose you by accident. And it wasn't for my sake."

What She Told Me

She closed the door again and let out a long breath.

"I'm sorry I've been so cold," she said. "I was angry, and none of it was about you. My date didn't really back out. I told my dad I didn't want to go at all, because I felt like I didn't fit in. He wouldn't let it go. Last night he told me he'd found someone to take me, and I assumed it was a pity arrangement he was paying for."

"I did say he'd make it worth my while," I admitted, my face burning.

"That's the part that matters," she said. "He talks about you all the time, Brent. He says you've worked since you were a kid. He says you've never taken a night for yourself, never gone to a dance, never done anything just for fun. He told me, 'That boy gives everything to everyone and asks for nothing.'"

I didn't know what to say.

"He wanted you to have one evening that wasn't a shift," she went on. "That's why he picked you. It was never for my sake. It was for yours."

My throat tightened. I had assumed I was just the reliable employee who could be counted on to fill a gap. I had never imagined he was watching me that closely.

The Night Begins

Georgia gave a small, embarrassed smile, the first one I'd seen all night. "So, I'm sorry I made you suffer through that ride. Can we start over?"

"Gladly," I said.

We walked in together. At first we were awkward, but she introduced me to her friends, and I made her laugh by admitting I had no idea how to dance. She tried to teach me, and I stepped on her shoes twice. By the end of the night, we were both laughing so hard we could barely stand.

It was the first time in a very long while that I wasn't thinking about bills, schedules, or what needed to be done tomorrow.

The Reward

On Monday morning, Sheldon called me into his office again. I expected an envelope with a little extra cash.

Instead, he handed me a folder.

"I'm promoting you to assistant manager," he said. "It comes with a real raise and regular hours, so you'll have time for yourself. I'll also cover the cost of any classes you want to take."

I stared at the papers, unable to speak.

"Georgia told me everything," he said with a gentle smile. "You gave her a good night. But you've been giving this place a good year. It's time someone gave something back to you."

When I told my mother that evening, she cried and hugged me so tightly I could hardly breathe. My sister asked if I was finally going to stop working so much. I laughed and told her I would try.

I learned something that year. Sometimes the people watching us notice far more than we think. And sometimes a favor that sounds like a request is really a quiet way of saying, thank you, we see you.
